title: Letter to Governor Abbott on responsible AI infrastructure in Texas
excerpt: Gotta love how all the companies' platitudes about sustainability become ludicrous as they begin burning natural gas at prodigious scales. But don't worry, "AI will solve climate change" so we can just pump extra CO2 now, right guys?
content_html:
Gotta love how all the companies' platitudes about sustainability become ludicrous as they begin burning natural gas at prodigious scales. But don't worry, "AI will solve climate change" so we can just pump extra CO2 now, right guys?

I am deeply, deeply cynical and honestly angry about these companies and their self-righteous protestations of being ethical, or public benefit corporations or whatever. Anthropic is benefiting from xAI's Memphis data center that is violating (previous, not anymore!) EPA standards, causing disproportionate impacts to nearby African-American communities. All the while, Ants appear to be floating on some higher effective altruist / B-corp plane. The little people and their petty concerns are just bumps on the road to RSI and ASI after all.


I think your anger would be better placed with the institutional barriers to building clean energy in America that prevent these infrastructure companies from doing the right thing

transmission via HVDC is extremely difficult to build due to land permitting and right of way laws

grid interconnections take 5+ years just to get approved, let alone built

only 2 nuclear power plants have been built since 1978, each taking over 10 years


Well, there's an admin killing clean energy so I think we know where that anger belongs. Dems suck too, but what can you do. One is worse, clearly.


As much as I wish it were different I think this would be the outcome under any administration. Natural gas in the USA is just stupidly cheap inflation adjusted, is energy dense, power plants require few land resources, pipeline infrastructure exists, robust and deep supply chain, etc. I don't hold much hope of the USA kicking the habit as it is such a competitive advantage. If we don't burn it locally it will be exported at a huge margin for geopolitical advantage. 1/3 of the CO2 reductions in the US power sector are due to renewables, 2/3 are from natural gas. Renewables would need to be backed up by additional gas capacity, although the average capacity factor would be reduced with a more robust renewable build out.


Biden was not paying companies to NOT build windplants.

No, the result would not be the same. Provably so.

Also, in fact, companies turned to Trump because democrats started to be serious about anti trust actions.


Billions of OUR dollars. Dumped into the MIC for Iran, wasting billions more of our dollars by surging energy prices. Then spending billions more to kill wind projects. Adding at least a billion to his own wallet.

How many billions of dollars will we allow this clown and his cronies to steal from us?


Are these companies expending any of their lobbying efforts or funds on this problem? Or are they just going to the easiest option? I'm not shedding any tears for the AI companies and their infra challenges. They're the ones driving a huge delta increase in energy use and emissions this coming decade, so their actions merit scrutiny and they are responsible for their actions and the resulting emissions that we will all suffer from. If I had my way, we'd stack an enormous carbon tax on all of them to force their hand.

Look, these companies are the ones selling a story of being benevolent (notwithstanding AI killing us all or putting everyone out of a job). And Anthropic is explicitly a B-corp. How does any of that square with taking any compute they can at any environmental cost?

The Memphis case to me is very illuminating: https://www.france24.com/en/live-news/20260811-memphis-ai-da...

But it's ok, they're EAs and gave $1M to a Memphis nonprofit on 'AI education', while spending a $1B/ month renting Colossus:

https://www.fox13memphis.com/news/anthropic-gifts-memphis-no...


yes, they are. they are hugely concerned that China has loads of power, and the US is incapable of keeping up

the biggest limiting factors for AI labs scaling are silicon, then electricity. they are acutely aware of this


People like Zuckerberg, Brin, Page and Musk have majority voting control of these companies.

They have amassed incredible power and vast fortunes in a time and era when doing so could only be done with great damage to the environment. Despite years of talk and superficial motions towards climate efforts these people have completely pivoted that signalling and have doubled down on endeavours that cause even more ecological destruction.

They have the power and means to do the right thing.

They chose not to.


since 2016 ish, big tech has measured infrastructure efficiency in watts, not dollars. that's because they made multiple long term deals for power that came up short

they want to build more power of any kind, ideally renewables. but the past decade has shown time and again that they can't build enough by any means


This is a collection of "OpenAI will boldly act in the abstract to provide air coverage for Texas leadership." With data centers under construction one would think they would have examples of successes or projects in progress available for reference. They'd claim credit if they had it so the silence is telling.

Big tech has consistently valued profit and growth above good stewardship; the onus is entirely on OpenAI to demonstrate that any of these claims aren't fluff with the projects that are already greenlit. When OpenAI presents plans to the communities prior to/alongside city counsels and drops the NDAs then there will be merit to this but our expectations should be somewhere between "super deep kola borehole" and "upper mantle".


Yeah if they were so committed to doing good, you'd think the billions of dollars they have spent would bear some evidence of that by now.


They must be "effective" "altruists".

The only way to do good is to first do all the bad and consolidate power, so you can then use all that power to do good, pinkie promise!


I've been to one EA meetup and it wasn't my thing but this seems nothing like the discussions I had. It's where I found out about GiveDirectly.

The biggest issue for me was the AGI/ASI doomerism. But then again, fast-forward five or six years and we've got "unaligned" AI agents blindly following reward functions...


Hey buddy, you're up against people who've only "learned about EA" as a third- or fourth-hand vibecloud around FTX.

Don't bring any of that firsthand knowledge here. You're also not allowed to reference any of the actual writing or pledges or organizations actually in the EA ecosystem. It's Twitter vibes or nothing, mmkay?


Seems you’ve rustled some jimmies. I’ve always thought effective altruism was a nice way to rationalize insatiable greed.


Consequentialism and to an extent Utilitarianism (since one is a subset of the other, it sometimes feels like philosophy is more concerned with naming things than explaining them but from the bit I've read those are the two biggest precursors).

AKA It's fine if I do locally horrible things if in aggregate I do more good than bad*

* by whatever metric of good I self select for - terms & conditions apply, much CO2 may be released.


It's funny, because as far as consequentialism, I feel like single-issue voters on all sides could use a bit more of that.

Of course, anything taken to extremes tends to get distorted.


FPTP results in a two party system where the sane response is often holding your nose and voting for the least worst candidate.

It's frustrating to vote for the person you disagree with least (by a little or a lot).


I have a weird take on that. When I was younger, I was like that. Now I find lacking the ability to "hold your nose" and do the best possible thing, in a less than ideal system to be simply selfish. As in, *I know there could be negative effects by me not voting, but I just can't sully myself." My virtue, above the greater good.

I would not usually even say that out loud, as I don't want to be accusatory. However, I think that's just the facts at this point. Hence, my statement about a bit of consequentialism being good.


I noticed the same thing about effective altruism. Its fans are really good at convincing themselves the most self-serving action amd goals are noble pursuits.


It suffers from an ends-justify-the-means trap where bad actions in the short term with the long term goal of good actions are justified by the fact that you, the actor, know your philosophy is the best way to enact positive change.

I'm happy to try and get already wealthy individuals on the train of effective altruism but it has been used to justify wealth concentration far too much and, to be honest, spreading money around is one of the most effective ways to enact real positive changes in the world since individuals know their own situations the best.


Imagine thinking that EA could actually cause people to concentrate more wealth than they would've otherwise lmao


I think that's the point. No one wants to be the villain in their own story. We all tell ourselves stories to paint ourselves as good. I don't think most people are evil, but I think most evil is created by people who have convinced themselves they are good.

So I see EA as a popular one of those stories. One that people can reinforce. Makes the world simpler than it actually is: climb the ladder, make money at whatever cost, there's no harm that you can do that can't be offset by giving it all away at the end. It is a vast over simplification and is inconsistent logic. If they used their own logic then they'd recognize helping people now also results in compounding effects. You fix the problems now, while they are small and manageable, rather than kicking the can down the road. Maintenance is a lot easier and cheaper than repair. But it also requires us to be nuanced and reflect on ourselves [0]

[0] there seems to be a great irony that those leading these big AI companies are not themselves able to deeply reflect on their own actions, yet ask the AI to. How can you design something that you aren't intimately familiar with?


I’ve yet to hear of effective altruism from anyone less wealthy me. Seems to be weirdly lumped among the rich.


To be fair to its adherents (of which I am not one), the so-called philosophy espouses maximizing income, so that one can later allocate that wealth efficiently. Working in a low-earning field which directly provides aid to those in need would seem to violate a core precept of 'Effective Altruism'.


> the so-called philosophy espouses maximizing income, so that one can later allocate that wealth efficiently

No it doesn't.

This is a thing that some EAs believe, but is definitely not a "core precept."


Intending to do good is a completely different beast to doing good. The promise of good later should always be discounted.


...provide air coverage for Texas leadership.

The GOP runs Texas. The governor, sec of state, AG, and both houses are republican. Since when have they ever wanted or needed air coverage?


The 2018 Senate race had a Democratic candidate lose by 2.6% while the economy for everyday Americans was doing much better. O'Rourke wasn't as good of a candidate as Talarico, and Cruz is a much better candidate than Paxton. That's not saying Cruz is good, just Paxton has almost as much baggage as Trump without the TV personality to whitewash it away. Republican strategists are expecting over 150 million to be spent on this race.

They will take anything they can possibly get at this point.

https://www.politico.com/news/2026/05/28/republicans-texas-m...


> Republican strategists are expecting over 150 million to be spent on this race

Imagine the assurances that are made to convince donors it's worth it. Who exactly bears the cost of unpopularity?...


Building stuff is good stewardship. We complain about NIMBYs. But with a few relatively modest regulations data centers can be quite friendly. They don’t generate traffic, congestion, etc. They don’t strain school or police infrastructure. Basically need some noise regulations. But the NIMBYs will kill it.


Not all things built are positive, so it can't be good stewardship just to build. And is the reason they don't strain infra because they don't meaningfully improve the community or its economy?


They need more than "we will prioritize". They need to act. They need to source power _today_, not just promise at some point in the future they'll probably fund a power plant, while raising rates for human consumers in the short, medium, and long term, for example.


Factories were originally located near housing (or vice versa) because the factories needed lots of workers. This doesn't apply to data centres. They don't need to be near anybody's home, so why should anyone be obliged to suffer their externalities? Just build your data centre somewhere else.


Data centers would be a benefit if my power bill and property taxes didn’t jump to subsidize the tax breaks my city gave them. I don’t want to pay for infrastructure multi-billion dollar companies should be funding.


Can you name any place where property tax rates on other residents were increased as a result of a tax break to a data center compared to the baseline of the data center not being there?


This seems like an entirely predictable outcome of data center builders and operators behaving like anti-social neighbors with noise just because no law prevented them from doing so.

Building a data center near homes and running your incredibly loud gas turbine generators 24/7 for months, destroying the property values and quality of life for the people living there, is a giant middle finger to the community they've moved into. I'm not saying the backlash banning them entirely rather than adding some additional regulations is entirely logical, but it's very understandable. And should have been eminently predictable.


> This seems like an entirely predictable outcome of data center builders and operators behaving like anti-social neighbors with noise just because no law prevented them from doing so.

The vast, overwhelming majority of data centers source power from the grid rather than continuously operating gas turbines, and the obvious response to the ones that do is to have a moratorium on gas turbines rather than data centers.


Citizens having a say in what is going on in their neighborhood is now controversial. Big brother knows best.


The ability of citizens to restrict or prohibit building in their jurisdiction is extremely strong, basically everywhere in the developed world[1]. There's not much they can do to affirmatively cause things to be built - that still takes capital and expertise - but local controls have stifled many, many, many parts of economic development and greatly skewed the economy.

[1] https://worksinprogress.co/issue/the-great-downzoning/


Citizens having a say in what is going on in their neighborhood is why housing in the bay area isn't expensive, they use that say to prevent the construction of new housing.


Prop 13 is why housing is expensive in California. Full stop. It was a bandaid over a wound and now the body has sepsis.


If that's supposed to explain it then why is housing also expensive in Massachusetts or Colorado?

It's ~18% more in California than Massachusetts but ~313% more in Massachusetts than Oklahoma.


NIMBY is largely used for housing development discussions and to contort it in support of developing data centers is incredibly intellectually dishonest.

If we're going to rebrand things to blur lines, I propose rebranding data centers to pedophile content hubs.

The rest of your argument is full of similar cherry-picking for dishonest discourse.


>NIMBY is largely used for housing development discussions and to contort it in support of developing data centers is incredibly intellectually dishonest.

No, it's frequently used in infrastructure discussions as well, eg. high speed rail or power transmission lines.


Or like property on the Texas Mexico border through which a wall is being built sealing off acres of private land from the owner.


That’s the opposite of NIMBYism. Public infrastructure getting built despite inconvenience to affected landowners.


That pointless infrastructure that has ‘inconvenienced’ landowners is also destroying a national park, so I guess we are all being inconvenienced. And funneled billions of tax dollars to private contractors.


Yes, building public infrastructure generally involves paying private contractors to do it. Who do you think builds government buildings?


Opposing new housing construction is bad in basically the same way that opposing data center construction is bad; and I'm happy to use the same word to describe both groups of people.


There is a much stronger argument for why housing should be built near existing housing than for why data centers need to be built near existing housing. Housing NIMBYs are being unreasonable because if they got their way the only new housing would be built in the middle of nowhere, which is clearly unworkable. Data center NIMBYs are arguing for much the same thing, but focusing on building data centers a good distance away from housing seems pretty reasonable.


> Data center NIMBYs are arguing for much the same thing, but focusing on building data centers a good distance away from housing seems pretty reasonable.

The trouble here is that the two things are related. It's easy to build a data center 50 miles outside the city. But because we don't allow higher density housing to be built, they instead have to build low density housing all the way out into what should have been rural land. Then you go outside the city to try to build something and instead of the neighbors being forests or fields of grain it's exurbs.


Why is opposing data center construction bad? People need housing, if there isn't enough affordable housing around, then opposing it can be bad. But also people who live there should have a say in what gets built near them, since they have to live with it.


The world and its people would continue to thrive if AI data centers magically vanished tomorrow. They are not necessary infrastructure. They're only necessary for wall street right now.


Sure, but we’re going to thrive more because of AI, just as we thrived more because of the Internet, cell phones, etc.


Infrastructure for what? To push AI, crypto and gambling on everyone? How about build this "infrastructure" in the back yards of billionaires? They should have plenty of land.


Oh please, running this site does not require any of these data centers. Nor new power plants.


I don't doubt you could host this site on any old Raspberry PI, but I guarantee it's hosted in a data center.


An extremely large dark black box. A haunted house on steroids. Not so quietly humming 24/7. Polluting the air from the large scale mobile gensets. Sucking in all the water and electric power so that the residential rates are going up and up.

I'm all for the datacenters, the more the better, it is the great race of acceleration of our civilization. Yet, it is pretty clear, and with history being the witness, that the tech-bros and MBAs will build it without any regard for the well-being of impacted communities. Thus we have the game of what communities will [be forced to] take a one for the team.

And this is why space base datacenters will be a thing :)


https://texas-connects.com/ is also running lots of commercials locally. But both this open letter _and_ the commercials intentionally skate around the resource needs.

> OpenAI will pay our own way and protect residential and small-business customers [...] OpenAI will work to support new power generation in Texas

Same with water, all of these projects want to leech on existing systems because they don't even want to entertain developing their own systems.

However, having worked inside Texas DCs for a long time now, I think it's just the burst that's the issue, not the concepts. Sadly they'll share our resources, but I think they should pay a premium on their energy compared to residential (but it's hard to reconcile this with other commercial ventures that do not).


This is a play to say something without putting down the ink that binds them.

> We will minimize water consumption and prioritize efficient cooling technologies, including closed-loop systems.

> We will work with local communities and water providers to ensure our projects are responsibly planned around available resources

I can promise you that I'll do everything to consider the needs and wants of others.

But I won't promise to take actions that take those wants or needs into account, much less even actually consider them.


The AI companies are spending close to a trillion dollars building data centers. On top of that, they’re now promising they’ll handle all environmental and power needs. I believe them, they probably will do that, thats not even too expensive. They need to however recoup this investment somehow, which is the fundamental problem with a technology like AI.

The only plausible way to recoup 1T is to automate large swaths of human jobs so that the companies stop spending money on humans, and instead give money to them. This is probably why the public doesn’t want AI, because AI in the rules of current society is perfectly designed to disempower and ruin humans, but is not actually capable enough to ruin humans in a state of nature.

Large massive data-centers that makes this economics work is not actually a fact of life, in a less stable country they’re actually a liability. If a countries technical prowess comes from a data center then an adversary just needs to bomb it to knee cap that country. On the other hand, if a companies technical prowess comes from a thousands of well trained humans, well that’s actually not easy to get rid of. They’re not stationary, they’re adaptable, they can pick up new skills quicker and cheaper. Any king would much rather invest in humans and not AI.

But in a country like US, where it’s hard to even imagine such instability, AI is perfect at outcompeting humans and ruining them short term, and ruining the country long term. No wonder, this seems to be turning out to become the most negative reaction the public has ever had to the advent of new transformative technology. Unfortunately I don’t think it will work, the AI companies are just going to steamroll them, steal their jobs and dignity and then put them on UBI and pay themselves on the back as if they did a good thing.


“ put them on UBI”

Never, ever will they do that. It’s the same bullshit like Musk telling people not to save for retirement. He can distribute his stock by now but instead he is grabbing on to more money.

If there will be UBI, it will be the absolute minimum to not starve. Basically the same as welfare now. No way they are going to share the wealth.


> If there will be UBI, it will be the absolute minimum to not starve. Basically the same as welfare now.

Well yeah. Realistically how much money do you think is available to hand out to every single person? Not enough for everyone to live comfortably. And if there was enough, you'd get large swathes of otherwise economically productive groups (aka the tax cattle schemes like this require) just deciding to drop out of the workforce.


Every single investment aimed at deploying labor-saving innovation has the impact of reducing the number of workers you need per unit of output.

That does not mean fewer jobs, it means that jobs graduate to higher order ones that produce more, and it means more goods/services chasing the fixed supply of workers, translating to deflation (higher real wages / more purchasing power).


OpenAI:

Commit to 117% of your datacenter power demand to be supplied by nuclear, wind, and solar, so it arrives the same day (or sooner) than your demand starts.

Because all these things require a grid, unlike on-site generators. Most grid equipment (specially high voltage transformers) are backordered and all companies have empty inventories. Unlike traditional companies these AI companies are deathly afraid of not getting to AGI first, so they can't wait.


If Virginia or Louisiana should profit by this then so be it. Californian land-use laws will have a net effect of -8 house seats against Texas. That is good. It should happen. If Texans will be poorer so Virginians will be richer, that is also good. May the American federal system reign forever. Allowing for states as experiments and letting them suffer their consequences is good. It is a machine for us to iterate on our present and future prosperity.


Polling shows a fairly bipartisan opposition to data centers, so it could encourage more states to join in with pauses of their own.


Side note: Now's a fantastic time get into industrial processes or oil & gas since all of the fake propaganda against buildings with computers in them has distracted people from facilities built on a daily basis that cause 1000x the pollution and noise of a datacenter.


You think the folks who are successfully organizing against datacenters can’t use the same techniques and support networks to do the same thing against other nuisance uses?


Not really - China doesn't care about other nuisance issues.

Look at how the TikTok kids (who went nuts for the Palestinians) don't give a crud about the Cubans.


At least many are aware of the viciousness shown by the current US administration against Cuban population.

At the same time, full blown humanitarian disasters, like the one that hit the Rohingya in Myanmar, people that were being thrown in pit and burned alive in the thousands, are completely unknown to the average adult in the west.


So where are the street protests for Cuba then? I marched for Gaza three times. I haven't seen a single one for Cuba.

I'm not saying empathy is a Chinese psyop. The empathy is real. But empathy requires awareness - and awareness IS controlled by the algorithm.


I take no position on the algorithm, I don't have enough context or subject matter expertise to speak authoritatively on the topic. My point is a single person can only care about so much, and can exhaust their compassion reserve. Can't be a passionate, engaged activist about everything.


You say obvious but provide no citations or data. “Some people say” or “it’s obvious” is not a sufficient foundation for an assertion.


i guess we’re seeing why your first account was nuked. if you’re failing to make a convincing point, you have to do better than replying with “LOL.”


Do you think that the issues deserve the same attention, or are you perhaps making a false equivalence?

As far as I’m aware, children aren’t being shot in the head and forcibly starved by an occupying force in Cuba. But to say that folks don’t care is clearly inaccurate.


I am making the fairly obvious point that Americans don't care about the Cubans like they did the Palestinians, despite the fact that the Cubans are directly suffering under the Americans, and in the case of the Palestinians it was indirect.


thinking that those two things need the same level of attention is for sure a false equivalence for reasons stated elsewhere. glad we got to the bottom of that one. further, we also saw that Americans do care, which is why we had elected officials there last month and can read about it through AP.


It is not really indirect, USA supports that genocide openly, polically and with arms.

But even more importantly, the care is result of years and years of leftist activism. Nothing to do with china, judt that awarness dont happen overnight.

Yours "if you are not active in absolutely everything, any action is invalid" is just a bad faith nonsense.


Well yeah nobody wants their local water supply to be either disintegrated into subatomic particles or polluted with every harmful substance known to man (whichever one they're supposed to do changes from day to day).


It's not just about water. It's about the noise, little to no benefit to the community besides a handful of jobs, air pollution where they're colocated gas turbines for power, and pushing up electricity prices. They are a net negative for most communities.

"Winning" in this context is simply slowing down permitting and construction until the capital bubble pops, at which point a great deal of these projects simply evaporate. And the bubble will pop eventually.

'Living in Hell': Data Center Neighbors Grapple With Noise, Air Pollution - https://www.usnews.com/news/national-news/articles/2026-04-2... - April 28th, 2026

Measuring the Impact of Data Centers in the United States Economy: Monetary Damage from Air Pollution and Greenhouse Gas Emissions - https://www.nber.org/papers/w35100 | https://doi.org/10.3386/w35100

> This paper quantifies the environmental externalities associated with electricity consumption by data centers in the United States, focusing on damages from local air pollution and greenhouse gas (GHG) emissions. Using facility-level data for approximately 2,800 operational data centers in 2025, combined with electricity grid characteristics and emissions data, the analysis estimates pollution impacts through the AP4 integrated assessment model and applies the social cost of carbon for GHG valuation. Results indicate that data centers consume roughly 250 TWh of electricity—about 5–6% of U.S. generation—and generate approximately $25 billion in gross external damages (GED), with a range of $10–$33 billion. These damages are highly geographically concentrated, with Texas and Virginia accounting for 30% of the national total. While GED comprises about 5% of industry GDP, this ratio varies widely across states, exceeding GDP in some regions. Planned data center expansion could increase electricity demand and associated damages by up to 85% in the near term. Despite these environmental costs, preliminary comparisons suggest that the damages attributable to AI-related energy use are small relative to potential productivity gains. [My note: potential gains]

Health implications of the rapid rise of data centers in Virginia: an exploratory assessment - https://www.frontiersin.org/journals/climate/articles/10.338... | https://doi.org/10.3389/fclim.2026.1648912

Unzoned means industrial. A slaughterhouse is MUCH worse than living next to a data center. If you want it zoned residential only do that.


It's isn't unzoned. It's zoned commercial. In VA, data centers are considered commercial, so allowed to be built by-right in existing commercial zones. Loudoun Co just updated their local zoning to override this and require re-zoning/approvals. (at least this is my understanding of the situation).

So, you buy a house, and think a small office park or strip mall might get built next door. Instead, it's a 6 story block that looks like the Borg, belches exhaust from on-site generators, and buzzes constantly making you think you have tinnitus or something.


You don’t seem to know much about where these datacenters are being built. They are usually greenfield sites, often in relatively rural areas where there may not actually be any local zoning regulations. Or this could be Russian propaganda, to manipulate US opinion against China in this case. What are your sources?

Beyond the construction they employ very little people and bring very little taxes at a gargantuan cost in resources.

The former middle class has entered the chat.

blocks.html_en: As much as I wish it were different I think this would be the outcome under any administration. Natural gas in the USA is just stupidly cheap inflation adjusted, is energy dense, power plants require few land resources, pipeline infrastructure exists, robust and deep supply chain, etc. I don't hold much hope of the USA kicking the habit as it is such a competitive advantage. If we don't burn it locally it will be exported at a huge margin for geopolitical advantage. 1/3 of the CO2 reductions in the US power sector are due to renewables, 2/3 are from natural gas. Renewables would need to be backed up by additional gas capacity, although the average capacity factor would be reduced with a more robust renewable build out.

sentences.en: As much as I wish it were different I think this would be the outcome under any administration.
sentences.zh: 尽管我希望情况有所不同，但我认为这将是任何政府领导下的结果。

sentences.en: Natural gas in the USA is just stupidly cheap inflation adjusted, is energy dense, power plants require few land resources, pipeline infrastructure exists, robust and deep supply chain, etc. I don't hold much hope of the USA kicking the habit as it is such a competitive advantage.
sentences.zh: 美国的天然气经过通货膨胀调整后价格极其低廉，能源密集，发电厂需要很少的土地资源，存在管道基础设施，强大而深入的供应链等等。我对美国戒掉这个习惯不抱太大希望，因为它是一个竞争优势。

sentences.en: If we don't burn it locally it will be exported at a huge margin for geopolitical advantage.
sentences.zh: 如果我们不在本地燃烧，它将以巨大的利润出口以获取地缘政治优势。

sentences.en: 1/3 of the CO2 reductions in the US power sector are due to renewables, 2/3 are from natural gas.
sentences.zh: 美国电力行业 1/3 的二氧化碳减排来自可再生能源，2/3 来自天然气。

sentences.en: Renewables would need to be backed up by additional gas capacity, although the average capacity factor would be reduced with a more robust renewable build out.
sentences.zh: 可再生能源需要额外的天然气产能来支持，尽管平均产能系数将随着更强劲的可再生能源建设而降低。

blocks.html_en:
Are these companies expending any of their lobbying efforts or funds on this problem? Or are they just going to the easiest option? I'm not shedding any tears for the AI companies and their infra challenges. They're the ones driving a huge delta increase in energy use and emissions this coming decade, so their actions merit scrutiny and they are responsible for their actions and the resulting emissions that we will all suffer from. If I had my way, we'd stack an enormous carbon tax on all of them to force their hand.

Look, these companies are the ones selling a story of being benevolent (notwithstanding AI killing us all or putting everyone out of a job). And Anthropic is explicitly a B-corp. How does any of that square with taking any compute they can at any environmental cost?

The Memphis case to me is very illuminating: https://www.france24.com/en/live-news/20260811-memphis-ai-da...

But it's ok, they're EAs and gave $1M to a Memphis nonprofit on 'AI education', while spending a $1B/ month renting Colossus:

https://www.fox13memphis.com/news/anthropic-gifts-memphis-no...

Are these companies expending any of their lobbying efforts or funds on this problem? Or are they just going to the easiest option? I'm not shedding any tears for the AI companies and their infra challenges. They're the ones driving a huge delta increase in energy use and emissions this coming decade, so their actions merit scrutiny and they are responsible for their actions and the resulting emissions that we will all suffer from. If I had my way, we'd stack an enormous carbon tax on all of them to force their hand.

Look, these companies are the ones selling a story of being benevolent (notwithstanding AI killing us all or putting everyone out of a job). And Anthropic is explicitly a B-corp. How does any of that square with taking any compute they can at any environmental cost?

blocks.html_en:
People like Zuckerberg, Brin, Page and Musk have majority voting control of these companies.

They have amassed incredible power and vast fortunes in a time and era when doing so could only be done with great damage to the environment. Despite years of talk and superficial motions towards climate efforts these people have completely pivoted that signalling and have doubled down on endeavours that cause even more ecological destruction.

They have the power and means to do the right thing.

They chose not to.

blocks.html_en:
This is a collection of "OpenAI will boldly act in the abstract to provide air coverage for Texas leadership." With data centers under construction one would think they would have examples of successes or projects in progress available for reference. They'd claim credit if they had it so the silence is telling.

Big tech has consistently valued profit and growth above good stewardship; the onus is entirely on OpenAI to demonstrate that any of these claims aren't fluff with the projects that are already greenlit. When OpenAI presents plans to the communities prior to/alongside city counsels and drops the NDAs then there will be merit to this but our expectations should be somewhere between "super deep kola borehole" and "upper mantle".

sentences.en: This is a collection of "OpenAI will boldly act in the abstract to provide air coverage for Texas leadership."
sentences.zh: 这是“OpenAI 将大胆行动，为德克萨斯州领导层提供空中覆盖”的合集。

sentences.en: With data centers under construction one would think they would have examples of successes or projects in progress available for reference.
sentences.zh: 随着数据中心的建设，人们会认为他们会有成功的例子或正在进行的项目可供参考。

sentences.en: They'd claim credit if they had it so the silence is telling.Big tech has consistently valued profit and growth above good stewardship; the onus is entirely on OpenAI to demonstrate that any of these claims aren't fluff with the projects that are already greenlit.
sentences.zh: 如果他们拥有的话，他们会声称自己有功劳，所以沉默说明了一切。大型科技公司一贯重视利润和增长，而不是良好的管理； OpenAI 的责任完全在于证明这些主张对于已经获得批准的项目来说并非无稽之谈。

blocks.html_en:
I have a weird take on that. When I was younger, I was like that. Now I find lacking the ability to "hold your nose" and do the best possible thing, in a less than ideal system to be simply selfish. As in, *I know there could be negative effects by me not voting, but I just can't sully myself." My virtue, above the greater good.

I would not usually even say that out loud, as I don't want to be accusatory. However, I think that's just the facts at this point. Hence, my statement about a bit of consequentialism being good.

blocks.html_en:
It suffers from an ends-justify-the-means trap where bad actions in the short term with the long term goal of good actions are justified by the fact that you, the actor, know your philosophy is the best way to enact positive change.

I'm happy to try and get already wealthy individuals on the train of effective altruism but it has been used to justify wealth concentration far too much and, to be honest, spreading money around is one of the most effective ways to enact real positive changes in the world since individuals know their own situations the best.

I think that's the point. No one wants to be the villain in their own story. We all tell ourselves stories to paint ourselves as good. I don't think most people are evil, but I think most evil is created by people who have convinced themselves they are good.

So I see EA as a popular one of those stories. One that people can reinforce. Makes the world simpler than it actually is: climb the ladder, make money at whatever cost, there's no harm that you can do that can't be offset by giving it all away at the end. It is a vast over simplification and is inconsistent logic. If they used their own logic then they'd recognize helping people now also results in compounding effects. You fix the problems now, while they are small and manageable, rather than kicking the can down the road. Maintenance is a lot easier and cheaper than repair. blocks.html_en:
This seems like an entirely predictable outcome of data center builders and operators behaving like anti-social neighbors with noise just because no law prevented them from doing so.

Building a data center near homes and running your incredibly loud gas turbine generators 24/7 for months, destroying the property values and quality of life for the people living there, is a giant middle finger to the community they've moved into. I'm not saying the backlash banning them entirely rather than adding some additional regulations is entirely logical, but it's very understandable. And should have been eminently predictable.

sentences.en: This seems like an entirely predictable outcome of data center builders and operators behaving like anti-social neighbors with noise just because no law prevented them from doing so.Building a data center near homes and running your incredibly loud gas turbine generators 24/7 for months, destroying the property values and quality of life for the people living there, is a giant middle finger to the community they've moved into.
sentences.zh: 这似乎是一个完全可以预见的结果，因为数据中心建设者和运营商的行为就像反社会的噪音邻居，只是因为没有法律阻止他们这样做。在住宅附近建造一个数据中心，并让令人难以置信的燃气轮机发电机 24/7 运行数月，破坏了居住在那里的人们的财产价值和生活质量，这对他们所搬入的社区来说是一个巨大的中指。

sentences.en: I'm not saying the backlash banning them entirely rather than adding some additional regulations is entirely logical, but it's very understandable.
sentences.zh: 我并不是说完全禁止它们而不是添加一些额外的法规的强烈反对是完全合乎逻辑的，但这是非常可以理解的。

sentences.en: And should have been eminently predictable.
sentences.zh: 而且应该是可以预见的。

blocks.html_en: Building a data center near homes and running your incredibly loud gas turbine generators 24/7 for months, destroying the property values and quality of life for the people living there, is a giant middle finger to the community they've moved into. I'm not saying the backlash banning them entirely rather than adding some additional regulations is entirely logical, but it's very understandable. And should have been eminently predictable.

Data center NIMBYs are arguing for much the same thing, but focusing on building data centers a good distance away from housing seems pretty reasonable.

blocks.html_en:
> Data center NIMBYs are arguing for much the same thing, but focusing on building data centers a good distance away from housing seems pretty reasonable.

The trouble here is that the two things are related. It's easy to build a data center 50 miles outside the city. But because we don't allow higher density housing to be built, they instead have to build low density housing all the way out into what should have been rural land. Then you go outside the city to try to build something and instead of the neighbors being forests or fields of grain it's exurbs.

blocks.html_en:
An extremely large dark black box. A haunted house on steroids. Not so quietly humming 24/7. Polluting the air from the large scale mobile gensets. Sucking in all the water and electric power so that the residential rates are going up and up.

I'm all for the datacenters, the more the better, it is the great race of acceleration of our civilization. Yet, it is pretty clear, and with history being the witness, that the tech-bros and MBAs will build it without any regard for the well-being of impacted communities. Thus we have the game of what communities will [be forced to] take a one for the team.

And this is why space base datacenters will be a thing :)

blocks.html_en:
https://texas-connects.com/ is also running lots of commercials locally. But both this open letter _and_ the commercials intentionally skate around the resource needs.

> OpenAI will pay our own way and protect residential and small-business customers [...] OpenAI will work to support new power generation in Texas

Notice how this very intentionally doesn't say they will work to support generating as much or more power than they will use? Because if they could do that, they would just generate their own power. It doesn't matter if they "pay their own way", they are now competing with households.

Same with water, all of these projects want to leech on existing systems because they don't even want to entertain developing their own systems.

However, having worked inside Texas DCs for a long time now, I think it's just the burst that's the issue, not the concepts. Sadly they'll share our resources, but I think they should pay a premium on their energy compared to residential (but it's hard to reconcile this with other commercial ventures that do not).

blocks.html_en:
This is a play to say something without putting down the ink that binds them.

> We will minimize water consumption and prioritize efficient cooling technologies, including closed-loop systems.

> We will work with local communities and water providers to ensure our projects are responsibly planned around available resources

I can promise you that I'll do everything to consider the needs and wants of others.

But I won't promise to take actions that take those wants or needs into account, much less even actually consider them.

blocks.html_en:
The AI companies are spending close to a trillion dollars building data centers. On top of that, they’re now promising they’ll handle all environmental and power needs. I believe them, they probably will do that, thats not even too expensive. They need to however recoup this investment somehow, which is the fundamental problem with a technology like AI.

The only plausible way to recoup 1T is to automate large swaths of human jobs so that the companies stop spending money on humans, and instead give money to them. This is probably why the public doesn’t want AI, because AI in the rules of current society is perfectly designed to disempower and ruin humans, but is not actually capable enough to ruin humans in a state of nature.

Large massive data-centers that makes this economics work is not actually a fact of life, in a less stable country they’re actually a liability. If a countries technical prowess comes from a data center then an adversary just needs to bomb it to knee cap that country. On the other hand, if a companies technical prowess comes from a thousands of well trained humans, well that’s actually not easy to get rid of. They’re not stationary, they’re adaptable, they can pick up new skills quicker and cheaper. Any king would much rather invest in humans and not AI.

But in a country like US, where it’s hard to even imagine such instability, AI is perfect at outcompeting humans and ruining them short term, and ruining the country long term. No wonder, this seems to be turning out to become the most negative reaction the public has ever had to the advent of new transformative technology. Unfortunately I don’t think it will work, the AI companies are just going to steamroll them, steal their jobs and dignity and then put them on UBI and pay themselves on the back as if they did a good thing.

blocks.html_en: The only plausible way to recoup 1T is to automate large swaths of human jobs so that the companies stop spending money on humans, and instead give money to them. This is probably why the public doesn’t want AI, because AI in the rules of current society is perfectly designed to disempower and ruin humans, but is not actually capable enough to ruin humans in a state of nature.

blocks.html_en:
Every single investment aimed at deploying labor-saving innovation has the impact of reducing the number of workers you need per unit of output.

That does not mean fewer jobs, it means that jobs graduate to higher order ones that produce more, and it means more goods/services chasing the fixed supply of workers, translating to deflation (higher real wages / more purchasing power).

sentences.en: Every single investment aimed at deploying labor-saving innovation has the impact of reducing the number of workers you need per unit of output.That does not mean fewer jobs, it means that jobs graduate to higher order ones that produce more, and it means more goods/services chasing the fixed supply of workers, translating to deflation (higher real wages / more purchasing power).
sentences.zh: 每一项旨在部署劳动力节约型创新的投资都会减少每单位产出所需的工人数量。这并不意味着就业机会减少，而是意味着工作岗位会向生产更多的更高阶岗位过渡，并且意味着更多的商品/服务会追逐工人的固定供应，从而转化为通货紧缩（更高的实际工资/更强的购买力）。

It's not just about water. It's about the noise, little to no benefit to the community besides a handful of jobs, air pollution where they're colocated gas turbines for power, and pushing up electricity prices. They are a net negative for most communities.

"Winning" in this context is simply slowing down permitting and construction until the capital bubble pops, at which point a great deal of these projects simply evaporate. And the bubble will pop eventually.

'Living in Hell': Data Center Neighbors Grapple With Noise, Air Pollution - https://www.usnews.com/news/national-news/articles/2026-04-2... - April 28th, 2026

Measuring the Impact of Data Centers in the United States Economy: Monetary Damage from Air Pollution and Greenhouse Gas Emissions - https://www.nber.org/papers/w35100 | https://doi.org/10.3386/w35100

> This paper quantifies the environmental externalities associated with electricity consumption by data centers in the United States, focusing on damages from local air pollution and greenhouse gas (GHG) emissions. Using facility-level data for approximately 2,800 operational data centers in 2025, combined with electricity grid characteristics and emissions data, the analysis estimates pollution impacts through the AP4 integrated assessment model and applies the social cost of carbon for GHG valuation. Results indicate that data centers consume roughly 250 TWh of electricity—about 5–6% of U.S. generation—and generate approximately $25 billion in gross external damages (GED), with a range of $10–$33 billion. These damages are highly geographically concentrated, with Texas and Virginia accounting for 30% of the national total. While GED comprises about 5% of industry GDP, this ratio varies widely across states, exceeding GDP in some regions. Planned data center expansion could increase electricity demand and associated damages by up to 85% in the near term. Despite these environmental costs, preliminary comparisons suggest that the damages attributable to AI-related energy use are small relative to potential productivity gains. [My note: potential gains]

Using facility-level data for approximately 2,800 operational data centers in 2025, combined with electricity grid characteristics and emissions data, the analysis estimates pollution impacts through the AP4 integrated assessment model and applies the social cost of carbon for GHG valuation. Results indicate that data centers consume roughly 250 TWh of electricity—about 5–6% of U.S. generation—and generate approximately $25 billion in gross external damages (GED), with a range of $10–$33 billion. These damages are highly geographically concentrated, with Texas and Virginia accounting for 30% of the national total. While GED comprises about 5% of industry GDP, this ratio varies widely across states, exceeding GDP in some regions. Planned data center expansion could increase electricity demand and associated damages by up to 85% in the near term. Despite these environmental costs, preliminary comparisons suggest that the damages attributable to AI-related energy use are small relative to potential productivity gains. [My note: potential gains]

It's isn't unzoned. It's zoned commercial. In VA, data centers are considered commercial, so allowed to be built by-right in existing commercial zones. Loudoun Co just updated their local zoning to override this and require re-zoning/approvals. (at least this is my understanding of the situation).

So, you buy a house, and think a small office park or strip mall might get built next door. Instead, it's a 6 story block that looks like the Borg, belches exhaust from on-site generators, and buzzes constantly making you think you have tinnitus or something.

blocks.html_en: You don’t seem to know much about where these datacenters are being built. They are usually greenfield sites, often in relatively rural areas where there may not actually be any local zoning regulations. Or when they are on brownfield urban sites, they are using “temporary” gas turbines that are incredibly loud and break all air pollution laws, taking advantage of loopholes and a complete lack of enforcement by the current EPA.

> It is a product of outside Chinese money being funneled into US politics to hobble the US in Artificial Intelligence

Or this could be Russian propaganda, to manipulate US opinion against China in this case. What are your sources?

Without evidence to the contrary, the prevailing narrative is more likely correct- people have been told by the tech titans that AI will change everything and they'll loose their jobs, so they don't like it.

In fact, whoever is saying the Chinese are tricking Americans may be trying to get more people to support US big-tech's AI build-out (or stock market bubble) by appealing to nationlism - that the Chinese will get us. A double cross.

blocks.html_en:
It is setting up the classic liability shift.

If you are just paying the bills and leasing the space, is it really your fault a datacenter some other entity built is sucking the water table of Levelland dry?

If I just use and don't own the data center, then how can I be held accountable for it's impact others?

sentences.zh: 它正在建立经典的责任转移。如果你只是支付账单和租赁空间，其他实体建造的数据中心正在吸干 Levelland 的地下水位，这真的是你的错吗？如果我只是使用而不拥有该数据中心，那么我如何对其他人的影响负责？

blocks.html_en:
Honestly, that sounds kind of arbitrary. Why should companies that use electricity be required to also produce electricity? This is what the market is for, so other Companies can produce electricity for money and other Companies buy that electricity.

And to which companies would this apply? Only Datacenters? There are other energy intensive industries too, should this also apply to them? And what is the cutoff for that? Does every bigger 21st century company also need to be an electricity company?

It would be less arbitrary if all negative externalities would be taxed (for example, carbon tax or noise pollution tax) and maybe prioritize households on the public grid.

sentences.en: And what is the cutoff for that?
sentences.zh: 其截止点是多少？

why are arbitrary rules a problem? if some company starts opening steel mills and its causing problems for the grid then the state can make all new steel mills build power generation. right now the problem is data centers so new rules are aimed at data centers.

carbon taxes dont work because all they do is make production more expensive, and businesses are always happy to pass on any extra costs to their customers. its the same with noise pollution and water use. the only way to actually stop them is direct regulation.

buying land does not give you the right to do whatever you want with it. stop worshipping property and markets and focus on real problems like limited number of business licenses, exclusivity contracts, long or lifetime post employment terms, weak competition rules and long waiting times at government offices. all of them go against the right to buy what you want, work for anyone who wants to take you or to start a business. thats the real economic freedom that is in danger today.

sentences.en: why are arbitrary rules a problem?
sentences.zh: 为什么任意规则会成为问题？

sentences.en: if some company starts opening steel mills and its causing problems for the grid then the state can make all new steel mills build power generation.
sentences.zh: 如果一些公司开始开设钢厂并给电网带来问题，那么国家可以让所有新钢厂建设发电站。

sentences.en: right now the problem is data centers so new rules are aimed at data centers.carbon taxes dont work because all they do is make production more expensive, and businesses are always happy to pass on any extra costs to their customers.
sentences.zh: 现在的问题是数据中心，因此新规则针对的是数据中心。碳税不起作用，因为它们所做的只是使生产成本更高，而企业总是乐意将任何额外成本转嫁给客户。

sentences.en: its the same with noise pollution and water use.
sentences.zh: 噪音污染和用水也是如此。

sentences.en: the only way to actually stop them is direct regulation.buying land does not give you the right to do whatever you want with it.
sentences.zh: 真正阻止它们的唯一方法是直接监管。购买土地并不意味着你有权用它做任何你想做的事。

sentences.en: stop worshipping property and markets and focus on real problems like limited number of business licenses, exclusivity contracts, long or lifetime post employment terms, weak competition rules and long waiting times at government offices.
sentences.zh: 停止崇拜财产和市场，关注真正的问题，例如有限数量的营业执照、排他性合同、长期或终身雇佣条款、薄弱的竞争规则以及政府办公室的漫长等待时间。

sentences.en: all of them go against the right to buy what you want, work for anyone who wants to take you or to start a business.
sentences.zh: 所有这些都违背了购买你想要的东西、为任何想要带你的人工作或创业的权利。

sentences.en: thats the real economic freedom that is in danger today.
sentences.zh: 这就是今天面临危险的真正的经济自由。

Say your 1979 Chevy is in need of a new 12V battery, but your car (for the purpose of the example) is under the NRC regulatory regime.

Can you just go to the auto parts store and buy a new lead acid standard issue battery? Definitely not. Well then ok, lets buy the most top shelf high-performance 2026 grade one. Also no.

The only battery you can use is the original one that came with the car in 1979. That's it. So now you have to pay a factory to produce a battery with a design from 1974. This battery easily costs $750k for all the custom engineering and low volume needed. And it is objectively worse by every measure to what is available at Walmart today for $50. So why do we have to use the original one? Because that is the battery that was certified, and certifying a new battery would take 10 years and tens of millions.

Again, I have pretty direct experience with this (a division of my company), and the situation above is a "translated" example of what goes down.

Maybe you call it "corner cutting" to use a new battery, but frankly I think you might be just speaking from the hip.

I very much realize it. I know companies are doing it. But the angry responses to my comment shows that literacy is lacking in Texas because I said it's political suicide to run on it as a platform.

Ken Paxton, who is running for Senate and currently serves as attorney general, proudly announced cracking down on "solar scams": https://www.texasattorneygeneral.gov/news/releases/attorney-...

Plus his campaign site makes no mention of supporting clean energy: https://www.kenpaxton.com/

I will repeat: it's political suicide to run on a platform of clean energy or education in Texas. That does not mean companies are not building clean energy. But politicians will not make it part of their platform during elections.

blocks.html_en:
> But the angry responses to my comment shows that literacy is lacking in Texas because I said it's political suicide to run on it as a platform.

If you really think Republican voters in Texas care so much about it, wouldn't the obvious play for Democrats be pointing out how much green energy these Republican politicians have allowed to be built under their watch? I think you're painting Republican voters with an extremely broad brush here and honestly, fail to understand what exactly they object to in the first place regards to green energy. Their main objection is being _forced_ to use it (or being chided by ivory tower know-it-alls) in contexts where they have certain preferences (like driving a big ass truck).

Not a single one is going to object to cheap energy so long as it doesn't degrade their current lifestyle. That's the point people like you forget when you're creating Republican straw men.

I know it’s cool with the kids to talk down Texas and its folks, but you might be surprised that Texas…

- produces more electricity from wind generation than any other US state.

- consumes more electricity from wind generation than any other US state (3x the next biggest, Iowa).

- has more installed wind generation capacity than any other state.

- energy usage leads all other US states by being comprised of 22% wind generation sources.

sentences.en: This is more of a lobbying attempt, Abbott just paused all new data center development in Texas until the state can audit them, they have an interconnection queue of about 474GW, ERCOT can't handle it that's more than 5x Texas's peak electricity demand.

blocks.html_en:
Abbot may very well be corrupt, but this letter does nothing to show that. The last thing I saw is ERCOT and PUCT will be involved with the auditing of the electricity and water usage [1] which would seem to indicate that it won't be the AI industry regulating itself. It seems like OpenAI wants to regulate itself, but Abbot is currently opposed to it. Could he change his mind? Of course, but the current situation appears to be the exact opposite of what you are thinking is happening.

[1] https://gov.texas.gov/news/post/governor-abbott-directs-comp...

blocks.html_en:
The main issue with wanting to block data centers in any specific location, is the hyperscalers will just move to building them wherever politics are most favorable. If protesters in your blue state block construction, they'll just build more in red states, giving the red states more leverage in how AI progress continues. If they are blocked across the board in the US, more will be build abroad, in countries that would never give credence to anti-datacenter movements that would stall economic growth.

The best option is to get everyone on the same page about AI benefits and hazards, and not be unrealistic about the way AI could shape up as a transformative element of human society.

content_html_zh: 当所有公司开始大规模燃烧天然气时，所有关于可持续发展的陈词滥调都变得荒谬可笑。 但别担心，“人工智能将解决气候变化”，所以我们现在就可以排放额外的二氧化碳，对吧？我对这些公司以及他们自以为是的道德或公益公司或其他什么的自以为是的抗议感到非常非常愤世嫉俗和真诚的愤怒。 Anthropic 受益于 xAI 的孟菲斯数据中心，该数据中心违规（以前，现在不再！） EPA 标准，对附近的非裔美国人社区造成了不成比例的影响。 一直以来，蚂蚁似乎都漂浮在某种更高效的利他主义者/B 型企业的层面上。 毕竟，小人物和他们的琐碎担忧只是 RSI 和 ASI 道路上的坎坷。我认为你的愤怒最好放在美国建设清洁能源的制度障碍上，这些障碍阻止了这些基础设施公司做正确的事情。由于土地许可和通行权法律，通过高压直流输电极其难以建设。电网互连需要 5 年以上才能获得批准，更不用说建造了，自 1978 年以来只建造了 2 座核电站，每座都需要 10 年以上好吧，有一个管理员正在扼杀清洁能源，所以我想我们知道这种愤怒属于哪里。 民主党也很糟糕，但你能做什么呢？ 显然，其中一个更糟糕。尽管我希望情况有所不同，但我认为这将是任何政府领导下的结果。 美国的天然气经过通货膨胀调整后价格极其低廉，能源密集，发电厂需要很少的土地资源，存在管道基础设施，强大而深入的供应链等等。我对美国戒掉这个习惯不抱太大希望，因为它是一个竞争优势。 如果我们不在本地燃烧，它将以巨大的利润出口以获取地缘政治优势。 美国电力行业 1/3 的二氧化碳减排来自可再生能源，2/3 来自天然气。 可再生能源需要额外的天然气产能来支持，尽管平均产能系数将随着更强劲的可再生能源建设而降低。拜登不会付钱给那些不建造风力发电厂的公司。不，结果不会一样。 事实证明确实如此。此外，事实上，公司转向特朗普是因为民主党人开始认真对待反垄断行动。我们的数十亿美元。 为伊朗倾销给MIC，能源价格飙升又浪费了数十亿美元。 然后再花费数十亿美元来扼杀风电项目。 至少给他自己的钱包增加十亿美元。我们会让这个小丑和他的亲信从我们这里偷走多少亿美元？这些公司是否在这个问题上花费了游说努力或资金？ 或者他们只是选择最简单的选择？ 我不会为人工智能公司及其基础设施挑战流任何眼泪。 他们是未来十年能源使用和排放大幅增长的推动者，因此他们的行为值得仔细审查，他们应对自己的行为以及由此产生的排放负责，而我们所有人都将遭受这一损失。 如果我有办法的话，我们会对他们所有人征收巨额碳税，以迫使他们采取行动。看，这些公司正在兜售仁慈的故事（尽管人工智能杀死了我们所有人或让每个人失业）。 Anthropic 显然是一家 B 型企业。 这些与以任何环境成本为代价获得任何计算有什么关系？孟菲斯的案例对我来说非常有启发性：https://www.france24.com/en/live-news/20260811-memphis-ai-da...但没关系，他们是 EA，并向孟菲斯非营利组织“人工智能教育”提供了 100 万美元，同时每月花费 10 亿美元租房巨像：https://www.fox13memphis.com/news/anthropic-gifts-memphis-no...是的，他们是。 他们非常担心中国拥有大量电力，而美国无法跟上人工智能实验室规模的最大限制因素是硅，然后是电力。 他们敏锐地意识到这一点像扎克伯格、布林、佩奇和马斯克这样的人拥有这些公司的多数投票控制权。他们在一个只能对环境造成巨大破坏的时代和时代积累了令人难以置信的权力和巨额财富。 尽管对气候努力进行了多年的讨论和肤浅的行动，但这些人已经完全转变了这一信号，并加倍努力，导致更多的生态破坏。他们有能力和手段做正确的事情。他们选择不这样做。自 2016 年起，大型科技公司开始以瓦特而非美元来衡量基础设施效率。 这是因为他们达成了多项长期电力交易，但最终未能实现。他们希望建设更多任何类型的电力，最好是可再生能源。 但过去十年一再表明他们无论如何都无法建设足够的这是“OpenAI 将大胆行动，为德克萨斯州领导层提供空中覆盖”的合集。 随着数据中心的建设，人们会认为他们会有成功的例子或正在进行的项目可供参考。 如果他们拥有的话，他们会声称自己有功劳，所以沉默说明了一切。大型科技公司一贯重视利润和增长，而不是良好的管理； OpenAI 的责任完全在于证明这些主张对于已经获得批准的项目来说并非无稽之谈。 当 OpenAI 在城市咨询之前/与城市咨询一起向社区提出计划并放弃 NDA 时，这样做会有好处，但我们的期望应该介于“超深科拉钻孔”和“上地幔”之间。是的，如果他们如此致力于做好事，你会认为他们花费的数十亿美元现在已经证明了这一点。他们必须是“有效的”“利他主义者”。做好事的唯一方法就是首先做所有坏事并巩固权力，这样你就可以使用所有这些权力去做善事，小指保证！我参加过一次 EA 聚会，这不是我的事，但这似乎与我进行的讨论完全不同。 正是在这里我发现了 GiveDirectly。对我来说最大的问题是 AGI/ASI 的末日论。 但话又说回来，快进五六年，我们已经有了“不结盟”的人工智能代理，盲目地遵循奖励函数……嘿，伙计，你面对的人只是“了解 EA”，作为 FTX 周围的第三手或第四手振动云。不要在这里带来任何第一手知识。 您也不得引用 EA 生态系统中实际的任何实际文字、承诺或组织。 要么是 Twitter 的氛围，要么什么都不是，嗯？看来你已经弄乱了一些吉米。 我一直认为有效的利他主义是合理化贪得无厌的贪婪的好方法。结果主义和一定程度上的功利主义（因为一个是另一个的子集，有时感觉哲学更关心命名事物而不是解释它们，但从我读过的来看，这是两个最大的先驱）。又名，如果我在当地做了可怕的事情，如果总的来说，我做的好事多于坏事**，无论我自己选择什么衡量标准 - 现在我发现，在一个不太理想的系统中，缺乏“管住自己的鼻子”并尽力而为的能力，简直就是自私。 就像，*我知道我不投票可能会产生负面影响，但我不能玷污自己。” 我的美德高于更大的利益。我通常不会大声说出来，因为我不想受到指责。 然而，我认为这只是目前的事实。 因此，我关于一点结果主义的说法是好的。我注意到有效利他主义也有同样的情况。
